script: AddBarEvent orbiting_spoon_start "Visit 'The Orbiting Spoon' diner" "Tucked into the back of the concourse hums 'The Orbiting Spoon', a massive, jury-rigged Domain-era culinary fabricator. There are no VIP rooms here; captains, officers, and grease-stained deckhands all crowd into cracked vinyl booths to eat warm, real food from the clanking dispenser chutes."

text: An emergency klaxon chimes from the jury-rigged fabricator as your cred-chit comes up empty. The machine's ancient Domain operating core overrides local lockouts, and its auxiliary relief chute clunks open with a dense nutrient brick and a fuel chit under Domain Relief Protocol 44-B. Austere charity from a forgotten age.
options:
10:orbiting_spoon_start:Stow the emergency supplies and take a seat in the mess hall
100:orbiting_spoon_leave:Take the supplies and return to the concourse

text: You walk past the bar counter to the corner housing 'The Orbiting Spoon'. Painted in regulation dull battleship gray with Hegemony Navy commissary seals, the jury-rigged Domain fabricator clunks rhythmically under the watchful eye of an armed commissary guard. Off-duty ratings eat at stamped steel benches in disciplined quiet under the smell of ozone, iron broth, and deck disinfectant.

The antique Domain fabricator shudders with a deep hydraulic clunk, venting ozone as its heavy brass dispenser tray slides out. A stamped metal platter holds a thick bowl of iron-rich soy stew, dense shipboard hardtack, and a scalding mug of chicory coffee. Austere, piping hot, and engineered to fuel a twelve-hour patrol burn.

You approach the acoustic-damped lounge where Tri-Tachyon has retrofitted the bar's Domain-era 'Orbiting Spoon'. Its antique casing has been gutted and replaced with sleek matte-carbon panels and biometric pay terminals, humming with clinical efficiency as corporate contractors dine at banquettes beneath the soft blue flicker of overhead stock tickers.

The modified Domain chassis hums at a high molecular frequency before unsealing its magnetic delivery hatch with a soft hiss of coolant vapor. A matte-black composite tray presents laser-seared synth-fillet beside an iridescent amino-gel matrix and chilled nootropic soda. Mathematically optimized to sharpen neural latency without gastrointestinal drag.

You find the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon' draped in crimson Lion's Guard pennants beneath glowing aquaculture display tanks of azure crustaceans. Diktat engineers have bolted high-pressure steam lines and external spice vaporizers to the Domain fabricator, while patrol captains converse over reef wine under the warm scent of clarified butter and charred peppers.

The brass-vented Domain machine roars like an orbital thruster as its steam pistons crack open. A polished platter emerges carrying split Volturnian lobster tail in fiery pepper butter, spiced aquaculture flatfish, and a carafe of purple reef wine. Rich, decadent, and a sharp reminder of the wealth the Lion's Guard bleeds to guard.

You duck into the quiet refectory alcove housing the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon'. The Church has solemnly decommissioned the machine's synthetic fabricator circuitry with holy lead seals, instead using its massive Domain-grade thermal induction core as a sanctified communal baking oven for real soil-grown loaves and stews.

Spacers watch with quiet reverence as the Church-consecrated Domain thermal unit unlatches its heavy insulated door. A fragrant ceramic bowl of barley and roasted fowl pie emerges alongside dense stone-ground sourdough, yellow churned butter, and steaming spiced cider. It tastes of fertile soil, woodsmoke, and honest labor.

You find the station's 'Orbiting Spoon' shoved into a rough subterranean bunker alcove. Cell fighters have hammered off every decorative panel, luxury circuit, and seasoning cartridge with heavy cold-chisels. Dented and scorched, the austere Domain machine simmers unspiced root broth over bare heating coils in the heavy silence.

The battered, chip-hammered Domain unit groans in protest, its uncalibrated chute sputtering grey penance broth into a dented tin mess kit beside boiled turnip mash and salted mutton. It is coarse, harsh, and completely unspiced: fuel meant only to keep a holy combatant alive and upright.

You step into a smoke-choked alcove cobbled together from scrap cargo hulls where the Pirates have chained the bar's Domain-era 'Orbiting Spoon'. Its warning lights are covered in black electrical tape, reeking of grease and sulfur while scarred corsairs slam dented tin mugs over games of high-stakes knuckle-dice.

Someone kicks the side of the junk-rigged Domain fabricator. It rattles violently, spits an acrid puff of grease smoke, and clangs open to dump sizzling blackened ribs, peppery fungal goulash, and a shot of caustic moonshine onto sheet metal. Fumes sting your eyes, but the heavy calories fuel a salvage run.

You find the bar's 'Orbiting Spoon' nestled behind colorful trade guild banners. League merchants have meticulously restored the Domain machine with engraved brass scrollwork and precision aroma-diffusers, its polished dispensing bays surrounded by ship captains and factors conversing over spiced olives and wine.

The polished Domain fabricator smoothly uncouples its pressurized amphora line with a chime, dispensing rosemary-rubbed lamb skewers, herbed flatbread, saffron waterfowl rice, and chilled citrus liqueur onto earthenware. Crisp, fragrant, and reflecting the flourishing trade routes of the League.

You step into a crowded alcove where an ancient, unpainted 'Orbiting Spoon' culinary fabricator rumbles in its Domain casing. Battered vinyl booths line the perimeter where tired independent haulers, freelance survey captains, and grease-stained mechanics hunch over steaming platters beneath flickering orange maintenance tubes.

The battered blue Domain fabricator hums reassuringly as its heavy dispensing hatch slides forward. A sturdy ceramic platter holds thick root-vegetable beef stew, golden waffles slathered in butter, and a mug of scalded black coffee. Honest, dependable spacer fare engineered to carry a crew through three consecutive hyperspace transitions.

You feed a cryo-crate of live blue-shell lobster into the raw-material hopper of 'The Orbiting Spoon'. The ancient machine's processors chime with forgotten Domain haute-cuisine protocols, steaming the butter-poached tails and cracking claws with surgical precision. The lavish aroma commands instant, reverent silence across the table.

You unseal vintage pre-Collapse luxury canisters into the fabricator's auxiliary gourmet bay. Centuries-old preservation seals pop as century-aged vintages breathe in decanters beside smoked delicacies. Sharing authentic Domain-era culinary luxury in this war-torn cycle is a profound reaffirmation of why we fight.

Heaped pots of thick communal porridge and grain stew are ladled out across the dockside refectory. Weary haulers, grease-smeared mechanics, and station ratings break bread together in solemn gratitude, sharing warmth against the cold void of the Sector.

$os_officerName rests both hands around their hot mug, exhaling slowly into the steam. ""Vessel readiness is within nominal parameters, Captain. I ran the point-defense gunners through interlocking screen exercises on the approach burn, cycling intercept vectors every forty seconds. When proximity alarms are screaming and flak bursts rattle the cockpit canopy, every fraction of a second counts. Sitting here over hot food, without a collision warning blaring in my headset... it's a rare gift. As long as our screening envelope holds and we don't overextend into crossfire, I'll keep our escort line intact.""

$os_officerName places their utensils down in precise alignment, studying the telemetry on their datapad. ""Logistics and drive readiness are secure, Captain. I had engineering recalibrate our thermal radiators during transit. Modern fleet actions aren't won by reckless valor; they are won by controlling engagement envelopes, weapon ranges, and heat dissipation. A commander who manages flux margins and standoff distances dictates the battle. Out in the black, an avoidable breakdown - whether an overheating coil or a crew sidelined by bad station provisions - is an unforced tactical defeat. We stay disciplined, and the ship stays intact.""

$os_officerName nods calmly, leaning back against the bench with weathered composure. ""Ship and crew are in fighting trim, Captain. Routine maintenance logs are cleared, magazine interlocks are checked, and the watch rotations are well-rested. Out in the deep hyper-lanes, fancy theories don't keep a battle line from buckling - sound training, dependable rations, and shared trust across the wardroom do. When the shooting starts, the crew looks to us for steady nerves. We've weathered worse storms than whatever lies past the jump-point. We're ready for the next burn.""

$os_officerName finishes their meal with swift, efficient focus and pushes the plate aside. ""Good fuel, Captain, but an idle warship gathers hull corrosion. Stagnation in port dulls gunnery crews and bleeds combat tempo. The enemy's battle line isn't broken by waiting for them to deploy their screen; you pin their vanguard, punch through their firing arcs, and dictate terms before their escorts can react. My gunners are dialed in, our capacitors are cycled, and we have the speed to seize the initiative. Put us at the head of the formation and let us dictate the tempo of the engagement.""

$os_officerName knocks back their drink, eyes glinting with grim amusement over the rim of the glass. ""Hot food, real smoke, and liquor that burns the throat - savor it while you can, Captain. I've spent two weeks drifting in an unpowered hull chewing frozen emergency paste with emergency klaxons howling in the dark. You learn fast that tomorrow isn't guaranteed in this Sector. When the shields flicker and armor plates buckle under heavy ordnance, victory belongs to whoever refuses to flinch. Give me a clear burn lane straight into their flank, and let's see which hull cracks first.""

$os_officerName nods respectfully across the table. ""Hot food and a quiet hour at the table go a long way out here, Captain. Weapons are calibrated, the bridge team is alert, and the ship is primed for combat deployment whenever you give the command.""

$os_officerName glances at the overhead structural ribs, lowering their voice. ""Defensive batteries at $marketName are heavy, Captain, but the approach corridor is congested. If hostile combatants stage an in-system raid, civilian lighters will choke the escape lanes. I've logged the firing arcs of their defensive platforms - if trouble starts, we keep our escorts tight against their point-defense envelope.""

$os_officerName reviews the patrol schedules on their datapad. ""Station security at $marketName maintains disciplined sensor sweeps, Captain, but their response flotilla follows predictable rotations. Furthermore, gantry fuel lines here are aging. An unforced fire in the docking ring could trap our hulls during an emergency scramble. I have ordered our watch to keep cold thrusters pre-heated.""

$os_officerName sips their coffee, watching the docking concourse with calm detachment. ""A well-ordered station, Captain. Garrison patrols are disciplined, traffic control is professional, and the orbital defense grid provides solid overlapping fire. As long as our transponders stay green and we respect local docking regulations, $marketName is a dependable staging harbor for the fleet.""

$os_officerName smirks toward the docking bay, leaning forward over empty plates. ""Station batteries at $marketName pack punch, Captain, but their perimeter picket is stretched thin. A fast strike vanguard could slip past their sensor buoys and hit the berths before their cruisers clear moorings. If we ever have to fight our way out of here, we seize the initiative and punch straight through.""

$os_officerName chuckles into their glass, eyes tracking an armed patrol. ""The local militia looks tough in their polished cuirasses, Captain, but they're sluggish. Their sensor grid has a blind spot right behind the solar array; I clocked it on our entry burn. If things go sour, we blow the docking clamps, gun the emergency thrusters, and let them try to catch our wake.""

$os_officerName nods thoughtfully over their mug. ""Defenses at $marketName appear adequate, Captain. Patrol craft are active and the station grid is powered. Still, it pays to keep our watch alert and engines warm whenever we're docked in the fringe.""

A deckhand leans in with a wry smirk. "Docking at $marketName is like house arrest, Skipper. ComSec inspected our airlocks twice and checked everyone's ident-chits. Still, the gantries have gravity and nobody tries to rob you. Just salute anyone wearing brass and keep moving."

An engine rating shakes their head, datapad in hand. "Spotless station, Skipper, but $marketName charges for every breath. An automated sentry billed me five credits just for gantry access. The crew loves the holo-ads, but nobody's signing a single corporate waiver."

A quartermaster snorts into their mug as brass marches buzz outside. "You can't walk ten meters in $marketName without Andrada's portrait glaring at you. The Lion's Guard acts like royalty, but fuel is dirt cheap. Nod at the banners and fill the tanks."

A deckhand smiles quietly into their mug. "It's peaceful here at $marketName, Skipper. No flashing holo-ads or bass vibrating through the decking. Smells like cedar and baking bread. We just kept our tech-scanners locked in the hold so the local deacons don't get nervous."

A deckhand glances toward the door, voice lowered. "Every minute at $marketName feels like sitting on a live torpedo, Skipper. Zealots along the gantry eyeing our shuttle like it's possessed. We have double watches posted at the airlock. Let's finish chow and undock."

A marine taps the table with a grin. "Rough town, Skipper. Docking fees at $marketName are whatever the local gang can squeeze out of you before someone pulls iron. Black-market ordnance is cheap, but watch your pockets and don't drink anything that glows."

A navigation rating chuckles over their drink. "The League loves a good show, Captain. $marketName is bustling with merchants preaching sovereign liberty while billing us for six separate dock fees. Still, the promenade is lively and the privateer gossip is worth every credit."

A hauler deckhand relaxes against the bench. "Real spacer territory here at $marketName, Skipper. No Hegemony patrols tapping bulkheads, no corporate lawyers, no holy zealots. Just worn freighters, honest traders, and spare parts. Good to dock somewhere you can actually catch your breath."

The crew grins proudly, glancing toward the gantries. "Looking over $marketName never gets old, Skipper. Our colors on the spires, our gunners on the station batteries, and no gantry shakedowns. It's home, built from our own salvage. We'll defend it to the last burn."

A senior rating sips their coffee, eyeing the concourse. "Every station has its headaches, Skipper, and $marketName is no exception. But the air cycles clean, docking clamps held, and the galley's hot. Watches are posted; we're ready to burn whenever you give the word."

An engine rating taps hardtack against the metal tray. "Skipper, you could fire this biscuit through a frigate's prow! But the stew is heavy and salty, and the chicory coffee wakes the dead. Beats shipboard algae paste any day of the cycle."

A deckhand eyes their empty plate with a smirk. "Weird corporate science, Skipper. The steak has zero gristle and that gel cube melted without chewing, but that cold nootropic soda cleared my skull instantly. Feels like combat stims without the heart flutter. Weird, but effective."

A gunner wipes chili sauce from their chin with a grin. "By the Lion, Skipper! That lobster tail was rich enough to start a mutiny, and the spiced skewers lit my tongue up. Chilled reef wine beats anything out of the ship's recycler."

A cargo hand finishes the sourdough crust with a quiet smile. "Real soil-grown barley and tender fowl, Skipper. On the ship, everything tastes of foil and recycled moisture. Fresh bread and hot cider make you remember why people bother living on planets."

A deckhand chews tough mutton, shaking their head. "This meat could patch a hull breach, Skipper. The broth has zero salt, but that bitter tea hit my veins like raw stim-fluid. Rough on the teeth, but it keeps a body moving under fire."

A mechanic licks rib sauce from their thumb with a laugh. "Those charred ribs fall right off the bone, Skipper, and the goulash has a kick. That moonshine stripped the grime right off my teeth. Greasy, hazardous, and thoroughly satisfying."

An astrogation mate smiles, clearing their plate. "Captain, saffron rice and crisp roasted duck beat anything in our ship's galley. The herbs on the lamb flatbread taste fresh, and that citrus drink clears the palate. The deck crew cleaned every tray down to the brass."

A veteran hauler digs into buttered waffles, coffee mug in hand. "Honest frontier grub, Skipper. Hearty beef stew, hot syrup, and black coffee strong enough to strip paint. No corporate fluff, just solid calories that keep a spacer standing on the deckplate."

The crew raises mugs in a quiet toast over cleared plates. "Skipper, harvest from our own colony, cooked by our own people... nothing beats it. We hauled the supplies and bled for those fields. Tastes like home, and it's worth every burn."

A seasoned deckhand scrapes their platter clean with a grin. "Captain, after weeks of vacuum-sealed starch and recycled tank water, hot diner grease and fresh coffee feel like Domain-era luxury. Cures bulkhead fever faster than any stim-shot in the med-bay. The watch is thankful."

The deckhands lean across the table, keeping their voices down. "Spacers at the freight depot say a Hegemony supply convoy went dark near the jump-point. No debris, no distress ping. High Command calls it drive failure, but dockers think something caught them in the storm."

A tech-rating leans close. "Overheard corporate reps in the concourse, Skipper. Tri-Tachyon lost contact with a research lab testing experimental phase coils out past the rim. They're posting quiet bounties for independent runners to recover the core logs: strictly off the books, no questions asked."

The crew snickers behind their mugs. "Spacers at the fuel pumps say the Lion's Guard is sweating, Skipper. Rumor is Andrada hasn't given an unedited broadcast in months, and fuel syndicates are fighting over clandestine pipelines. If the old man drops, Askonia becomes a warzone."

A deckhand leans in, whispering. "Pilgrims at the shrine say the Synod is uneasy, Skipper. Outer communes report strange lights dancing in the night sky, and elders warn caravans off Path border systems. Pious folk call it an omen; spacers think it's stealth warships."

A deckhand murmurs tensely. "Overheard cell fighters near the airlock, Skipper. The Path is moving improvised munitions toward core manufacturing hubs, preparing strikes against automated facilities. They're telling believers to hoard fuel and lead shielding. If their strike packs show on sensors, we shouldn't linger."

A marine taps the table with a grin. "Word at the dive bar is a heavy League transport lost drive containment in hyperspace near Magec. Three raider wolfpacks are already racing for the carcass, and dockside fences are dumping stolen torpedoes for dirt cheap."

A navigation rating sips their drink. "Kazeron is squeezing member worlds for emergency defense tithes, claiming Hegemony aggression is imminent. Half the League colonies are refusing and hiring mercenary flotillas instead. Privateer bounties are high if you're looking for gun work, Captain."

A scavenger deckhand leans in. "An independent scrapper limped into port with scorched radiators. Claimed they picked up an ancient Domain signal echoing out from an uncharted rim system. Half the prospectors on the gantry are buying fuel to race out there before corporations notice."

The crew grins around the table. "Skipper, freight skippers at the exchange are talking up $marketName. Lower tariffs and real security are pulling independent trade from Core routes. Several veteran engineers on the gantry were already asking our deckhands how to sign on with us."

A deckhand leans in, tracing a line on the table. "Gantry chatter is nervous, Skipper. Haulers coming off the hyper-lanes claim automated contacts shadowed them past the fringe, broadcasting dead Domain transponder codes. The fringe is getting restless. Best keep our point defense manned."
You leave the mess hall table, drop your meal chits at the commissary hatch, and step back out into the bustling concourse, refreshed and ready for the next burn into hyperspace.

You take a seat among the off-duty watchstanders in the mess hall. Over steaming platters of diner food, seasoned deckhands and rookie spacers talk through fuel margins, reactor baffle cleanings, and close calls from previous jumps. Spacers exchange advice on keeping sensor arrays aligned and catching micro-fractures before hull alarms sound. The camaraderie and shared lessons steady the whole crew.
